title: Origins and growth of Hinduism
summary: Hinduism has no single founder and no single date of origin. The Met describes mixed origins: one strand runs back to the Vedas, Sanskrit hymns to deities of the natural elements, and another to the beliefs of indigenous peoples. The Vedic period is commonly dated about 1500 to 500 BCE, and the Vedic teachings, which include the Upanishads, were passed on orally long before they were written down. Hinduism in a form close to today's emerged around the start of the Christian era.

uncertainty.note: Hinduism has no founder or fixed starting date; the range is the conventional Vedic period. WHE gives c. 1500 to c. 500 BCE; the Gale entry dates the Vedic literature to about 1400 to 400 BCE; the Met places the emergence of Hinduism in a form close to today's around the start of the Christian era.
